question: Can the unchanged final A003 evaluations run one at a time with enforced external budget deadlines and verified recovered-checkpoint lineage?
hypothesis: A CPU supervisor can bound a stuck evaluator without depending on GPU progress, preserve raw outputs, and account for the complete owned child lifetime without double-counting its internal interval.

sources.sections: Popen poll/wait, TimeoutExpired, file redirection, terminate and kill
sources.consequence: A wait timeout is not child termination. Redirect to a file and keep the owned Popen handle; explicitly terminate, wait and if necessary kill at the declared deadline.

sources.version: official API read2026-11-15; local supervisor Python psutil5.9.8 is_running/terminate/kill source inspected
sources.sections: Process identity and PID reuse; is_running, create_time, terminate, kill
sources.consequence: Signals require matching PID, creation time, command and cwd. Do not signal an unrelated trainer, desktop process or reused PID.
Use a monotonic deadline fixed at admission, plus current ledger remaining allowance; wall-clock changes cannot extend the original permitted duration.
Use the existing shared ledger lock for admission/closure. Refuse other open intervals. Close the owned outer interval and only its uniquely matched child interval after confirmed child exit.
Keep the A003 train-only frozen-weight calibration and population-statistics inference unchanged; operational completion is separate from numerical validity.

sources.sections: Floating point and batched versus sliced computations
sources.consequence: Retain the selected float64/math policy and original tolerances. Zero process exit cannot substitute for reviewing every numerical comparison.

differences: An external operational supervisor replaces the retired six-live-PID queue for the recovered paths. It does not modify the pinned A003 evaluator, precision, samples, calibration, tolerance or order. CPU tests use temporary fake ledgers and owned harmless subprocesses only.
contrary_evidence: A time-limited exit cannot identify the source of a GPU stall, and a zero exit cannot establish numerical or scientific success. OS scheduling or an uninterruptible kernel task can exceed a requested deadline; report actual time and leave unresolved intervals open rather than claiming a hard real-time guarantee.

protocol.scope: Only the six declared A003 final evaluations, launched individually after all six A014 runs and actual A015 final audits pass review. No concurrent GPU work, automatic successors, scientific auto-review or changes to original/gated source.
protocol.admission: Refuse live repository trainers, missing/stale final reviews, nonterminal/nonzero A014 executions, changed source/config/data/final hashes, foreign open ledger intervals, existing result directories and another compute process. Bind all six A015 audits to A014 terminal results; each A014 completion review must include final_audit_review and final_audit_review_sha256. Require the preceding A003 case's passing review before a later case.
protocol.budget: Use the existing48-hour additional-device ledger and the4-hour A allocation. Deduct the union of all prior A-prefixed intervals from4 hours. Add an outer A016 interval covering child startup through confirmed exit; overlapping internal A003 time is charged once by union. Original training remains excluded. Reserve45 seconds for cleanup; refuse admission with no positive work allowance. No budget reset or increased allowance.
protocol.supervision: The deadline is the smaller of remaining A and global allowances minus45 seconds, measured monotonically from ledger admission. Recheck the current ledger at most every30 seconds. At exhaustion send SIGTERM to the exact owned identity, wait30 seconds, then SIGKILL only if needed and wait10 seconds. On supervisor error clean up that same child. Keep accounting open if termination is unconfirmed. Preserve return code, elapsed time, signals, errors and raw result/manifest hashes; no automatic retry.
protocol.classification: A budget-deadline stop is budget_incomplete. A nonzero exit or unresolved process/accounting error is technical_blocked. A successful child remains awaiting_literature_review. Retain the raw A003 result even if operational supervision fails. Never manufacture a passing A003 review.
protocol.verification: CPU suite checks interval union, A/global admission limits, foreign-open refusal, exact owned inner-interval closure while preserving closed/foreign rows, refusal to close a live child, PID identity mismatch without a signal, normal child success/failure, SIGTERM timeout cleanup and SIGKILL escalation. The real CLI must refuse the current live trainer before output creation or shared-ledger mutation. Test ledgers must be temporary and never replace the shared ledger.
protocol.review: Review software results against the technical sources before actual use. For each actual A003 result, revisit BN and numerical literature, inspect all checks and review exact result/calibrated hashes before a successor. A016 execution also receives its own operational review. Failed/incomplete outcomes remain explicit.

success: The tested wrapper enforces admission, identity, deadline and accounting rules without changing the experiment. Actual numerical success is determined separately by A003 at its existing tolerances.
stop: Any failed lineage/review/budget/exclusivity guard refuses launch. An owned child's resource or technical stop blocks successors pending literature review. Do not reset the device, alter source, weaken numerical gates or treat a timed-out experiment as a scientific negative.

resources.training_device: No training; unchanged A003 on dedicated GPU, declared CPU parity reference only
